definition_zh: 蜂蜜；甜心；亲爱的（称呼）
definition_en: the sweet sticky food made by bees, or a loving word for someone dear to you
core_image: 琥珀色的一勺金黄：甜得粘住舌尖，也甜在称呼里
scene: 面包刚烤好，奶奶抹上一层金黄的蜂蜜。 Grandma spread some honey on the warm bread.
sceneCN: 这里 honey 是「蜂蜜」（第 1 个义项：蜜蜂酿的甜食）；奶奶往温热的面包上抹蜂蜜。

derivatives.zh: honey + bee → 蜜蜂
honey + moon → 蜜月（新婚第一个月最甜）
honey + -ed → 甜言蜜语的；加了蜜的
honey + pot → 蜜罐（引诱人的甜饵）

senses.title: The sweet food made by bees
senses.definition: a sweet, thick, golden food that bees make from flower nectar
senses.definitionCN: 蜜蜂用花蜜酿成的浓稠香甜的金黄色食物
senses.example: Bees store honey in the cells of the comb.
senses.exampleCN: 蜜蜂把蜂蜜储存在蜂巢的巢室里。
senses.why: The core sense is the sweet liquid itself, straight from the hive.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是蜂巢里取出的那勺甜液本身。

senses.title: A loving name for a dear person
senses.definition: a word you call someone you love, especially a partner or child
senses.definitionCN: 对所爱之人的称呼，多用于伴侣或孩子
senses.example: Honey, dinner is ready!
senses.exampleCN: 亲爱的，吃饭啦！
senses.why: The sweetness of the food became the sweetness of a person you call with love.
senses.whyCN: 食物的甜变成了人的甜：用一声「甜」呼唤所爱之人。

senses.title: Sweet flattery
senses.definition: pleasant words used to persuade someone, as in honeyed words
senses.definitionCN: 用来劝诱别人的动听话，如 honeyed words
senses.example: He won the deal with honeyed words and small promises.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠甜言蜜语和小许诺拿下了这笔生意。
senses.why: Sweet speech coats the tongue like honey coats bread, making hard words easy to swallow.
senses.whyCN: 甜话裹住舌头，就像蜂蜜裹住面包，让难听的话也容易咽下。

intro.en: Honey is an Old English word, hunig, from a Germanic root; Latin mel names the same sweet thing from another root.
intro.cn: honey 是古英语词 hunig，来自日耳曼词根；拉丁语 mel 用另一个词根命名同一种甜物。

items.en: Old English hunig named the bee’s sweet store; the -ig ending looks like the adjective ending -y.
items.cn: 古英语 hunig 指蜜蜂储存的甜物，词尾 -ig 与形容词后缀 -y 相像。

items.en: The root is Germanic: Dutch honig and German Honig keep the same shape.
items.cn: 词根属日耳曼语族：荷兰语 honig、德语 Honig 形状相同。

items.en: In Middle English the spelling settled as honey, and the loving use began to appear.
items.cn: 中古英语定型为 honey，爱的称呼用法开始出现。

items.en: Modern English added honeymoon in the sixteenth century and honeyed words later.
items.cn: 现代英语在十六世纪造出 honeymoon，后来又有了 honeyed words。

items.en: Latin mel is the classical name for honey; it builds mellifluous, flowing with honey.
items.cn: 拉丁 mel 是蜂蜜的古典名称，派生出 mellifluous（甜美如蜜流）。

note.en: Group one shows the honey compounds; group two shows the sweet and loving near words.
note.cn: 第一组是 honey 复合词；第二组是表示甜与亲昵的近义词。

normalIntro.en: Use the visible compounds and the sweet family.
normalIntro.cn: 用看得见的复合词与甜味词族记 honey。

normal.en: honey + moon = the sweetest first month of marriage
normal.cn: honey + moon＝婚姻最甜的第一个月＝蜜月。

normal.en: honey + bee = the bee that makes honey
normal.cn: honey + bee＝酿蜜的蜂＝蜜蜂。

normal.en: as sweet as honey describes taste and speech
normal.cn: as sweet as honey 既能说味道，也能说嘴甜。

normal.en: Honey, I am home: one word warms the door
normal.cn: Honey, I am home：一个词把门口都焐热了。

normal.en: mellifluous means flowing with honey, sweet to hear
normal.cn: mellifluous 字面是「流着蜜的」，形容声音甜美。

abstract.en: Picture one golden drop sliding slowly down the spoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴金黄缓缓顺着勺沿滑落——蜂蜜的慢与稠。

abstract.en: Picture a hive humming like a small warm engine.
abstract.cn: 想象蜂箱像一台温热的小引擎嗡嗡作响。

abstract.en: Feel a sweet word coat a hard sentence until it slides down.
abstract.cn: 感受一句甜话裹住生硬的句子，让它顺利下咽。

examples.en: Bees make honey from the nectar of flowers.
examples.cn: 蜜蜂用花蜜酿出蜂蜜。

examples.en: Good words are like honey to a tired heart.
examples.cn: 好话对疲惫的心就像蜂蜜一样甜。

examples.en: They spent their honeymoon by the sea.
examples.cn: 他们在海边度过了蜜月。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈尼」——喝一口蜜，甜得「哈」一声喊「尼（你）真甜」，这就是 honey（蜂蜜；甜心）。

root: honey 来自古英语 hunig，属日耳曼语族本族词，荷兰语 honig、德语 Honig 同源；拉丁语用另一词根 mel 命名蜂蜜，派生 mellifluous 等。

sensesIntro.en: From the bee’s sweet store, honey spreads to loving names and to flattery.
sensesIntro.cn: honey 从蜂巢的甜物出发，扩展为亲昵称呼，再到甜言蜜语。

intro.cn: honey 是日耳曼本族词，主要用作复合词的前半。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mel 是古典对照词，派生出 melon、mellow 与 mellifluous。

items.example: The jar of honey was almost empty.

items.exampleCN: 一只蜜蜂一天访问数百朵花。

items.meaning: a sweet trap to lure someone

definition_zh: 交通；往来车辆；运输量；（非法）交易
definition_en: the vehicles moving along a road, or the movement of goods and people, and also illegal dealing in goods
core_image: 一条被车塞满的路，车灯一盏接一盏亮着
scene: 傍晚的高架桥上，车一辆贴着一辆，红色的尾灯一直排到看不见的地方。 We left early to avoid the traffic on the ring road.
sceneCN: 这里 traffic 是「交通、往来车辆」（第 1 个义项：路上行驶的车辆及其流动）；句意为我们早早出发，以避开环路拥堵的车流。

pos.zh: 名词：交通；车流；运输；（非法）交易

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成（双写 k），义为「非法贩运者」
由动词加 -ing 构成（双写 k），义为「非法贩运」

senses.title: Vehicles moving on roads
senses.definition: the cars, buses, and lorries moving along a road at any one time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻在道路上行驶的汽车、公交与货车
senses.example: The traffic was so heavy we walked the last mile.
senses.exampleCN: 车流太堵，最后一英里我们是走过去的。
senses.why: The word comes from an Italian verb of trading, and traffic on a road is simply the commerce moving there.
senses.whyCN: 本词来自意大利语「做买卖」的动词，路上的车流就是在这条路上流动的商贸。

senses.title: The movement of goods and people
senses.definition: the movement of people or goods by road, rail, sea, or air
senses.definitionCN: 人或货物通过公路、铁路、海路或航空的流动
senses.example: The port handles freight traffic from three continents.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口处理来自三大洲的货运。
senses.why: Once the word means movement, it can measure that movement in tonnes and passengers rather than count cars.
senses.whyCN: 一旦本词表示流动，就可以用吨位和客流来度量这种流动，而不只是数车。

senses.title: The number of visitors to a place
senses.definition: the amount of people or data passing through a place or system in a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内通过某地或某系统的客流或数据量
senses.example: The website had record traffic after the article appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇文章出现后，网站访问量创了纪录。
senses.why: A modern network also has traffic, since messages move through it as goods move along roads.
senses.whyCN: 现代网络也有 traffic，因为消息在网络中的流动正如货物在路上的流动。

senses.title: Illegal dealing in goods
senses.definition: the buying and selling of something illegal, such as drugs or stolen goods
senses.definitionCN: 买卖毒品、赃物等违法物品
senses.example: The police broke up a traffic in stolen bicycles.
senses.exampleCN: 警方打掉了一桩被盗自行车的交易。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: trade itself, which turns dark when the goods are forbidden.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的含义：贸易本身，当货物被禁时就变成了黑色交易。

senses.title: To deal illegally
senses.definition: to buy and sell something illegal, used mostly in the form trafficking
senses.definitionCN: 买卖违法物品，多见于 trafficking 这一形式
senses.example: They were charged with trafficking in protected birds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们被控非法买卖受保护的鸟类。
senses.why: The verb keeps only the unlawful branch of the old trade meaning, so it almost always names a crime.
senses.whyCN: 动词只保留了旧「贸易」义中不合法的那一支，因此几乎总指犯罪。

intro.en: Traffic comes from Italian traffico, trade, probably from trafficare, to trade, with a possible ultimate link to a word for grinding or moving about.
intro.cn: traffic 来自意大利语 traffico（贸易），大概出自 trafficare（做买卖），其更远来源可能与表示「碾磨、往来」的词有关。

items.en: The deeper source is disputed; some trace it to a Vulgar Latin verb of moving goods about, others to an Arabic root.
items.cn: 更深来源有争议，有人追溯到通俗拉丁语表示搬运货物的动词，也有人主张来自阿拉伯语词根。

items.en: Italian traffico means commerce or trade, often with a hint of dealings that are not quite clean.
items.cn: 意大利语 traffico 意为商业、贸易，常带着「不太干净的买卖」的暗示。

items.en: French trafic carries the word into wider use in the sixteenth century, still meaning trade.
items.cn: 十六世纪法语 trafic 把这个词带进更广的使用，仍指贸易。

items.en: English adopts traffic for trade, and the phrase traffic in goods becomes common.
items.cn: 英语借入 traffic 表示贸易，traffic in goods 一类说法变得常见。

items.en: In the nineteenth century, with railways and busy streets, the word shifts to the movement of vehicles.
items.cn: 十九世纪随着铁路与繁忙街道的出现，这个词转向指车辆的流动。

items.en: The unlawful sense survives mainly in phrases such as drug trafficking and the verb traffick.
items.cn: 不合法之义主要保存在 drug trafficking 一类说法与动词 traffick 中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the traffic family, and the near-meaning group gathers words for vehicles, congestion, and trade.
note.cn: 形近组收集 traffic 词族，近义组收集表示车辆、拥堵与贸易的词。

illegal trading

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the Italian trade origin, from the uncountable noun, and from the two branches of road flow and illegal dealing.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从意大利语「贸易」来源、不可数名词属性以及「车流」与「非法交易」两条分支入手。

normal.en: Traffic began as trade, so the cars on a road are goods of a sort, moving.
normal.cn: traffic 原是贸易，所以路上的车某种意义上也是流动的货物。

normal.en: As a noun traffic has no plural: say heavy traffic, not many traffics.
normal.cn: 作名词时 traffic 没有复数：说 heavy traffic，而不说 many traffics。

normal.en: The verb doubles the k: trafficked, trafficking, trafficker.
normal.cn: 动词要双写 k：trafficked、trafficking、trafficker。

normal.en: Traffic lights, traffic jam, traffic accident: the word stands in front to say where the flow is short.
normal.cn: traffic lights、traffic jam、traffic accident，本词放前面说明流动受阻之处。

normal.en: Traffic in drugs is the old trade sense surviving in criminal form.
normal.cn: traffic in drugs 是古老贸易义以犯罪形式留存下来的样子。

abstract.en: Picture a river of red tail lights that moves only a few metres at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一条红色尾灯的河，每次只前挪几米。

abstract.en: Think of ants on a sugar trail, and then make the ants into lorries.
abstract.cn: 想糖迹上的一队蚂蚁，再把蚂蚁换成货车。

abstract.en: Traffic is other people's decisions taking up room on your road.
abstract.cn: 交通就是别人的决定占了你路上的位置。

examples.en: There was a lot of traffic on the coast road this morning.
examples.cn: 今天早上沿海路上车很多。

examples.en: The new traffic lights made the junction much safer.
examples.cn: 新的红绿灯让这个路口安全多了。

examples.en: He was arrested for trafficking in stolen goods.
examples.cn: 他因买卖赃物被捕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「戳非克」——车子一辆戳着一辆，挤得谁也过不去，就是交通堵。

root: 意大利语 traffico（贸易）→ 法语 trafic → 英语 traffic（贸易 → 车流）。更远来源有争议，可能与表示搬运、往来的词有关。词族有 trafficker、trafficking。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the oldest sense of trade, then turns into the movement of goods, then into the vehicles themselves, then into the flow through networks, and ends with the criminal branch of dealing in forbidden goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词从「贸易」这一最古老含义出发，转为货物流动，再转为车辆本身，再转为网络中的流量，最后落在买卖违禁品的犯罪分支上。

core.cn: 核心意象：一条挤满移动车辆的路。

branches.en: The cars and buses on the road.
branches.cn: 路上的汽车与公交。

branches.en: The freight and passengers moved.
branches.cn: 被运送的货物与旅客。

branches.en: The volume passing through a place.
branches.cn: 通过某地的人流量。

branches.en: Trade in forbidden goods, noun and verb.

branches.en: The crowded road that started the circle.
branches.cn: 开启这一循环的拥堵路面。

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing from Italian with no productive suffix, and its small family uses -er and -ing with a doubled k.
intro.cn: 本词是经法语借入的意大利语词，没有能产后缀，其小词族用 -er 与 -ing，并双写 k。

items.exampleCN: 贸易义保留在 traffic in drugs 中。

items.exampleCN: 交通繁忙让整座城市变慢。

definition_zh: 我们自己；我们亲自；独自；私下地
definition_en: the reflexive pronoun used when the subject we acts on itself, and the emphatic form that stresses that we personally did something
core_image: 几个人围着一张搬进教室的旧桌子，四下张望，确认没有别人在帮忙
scene: 周末的教室空了下来，几个人自己搬桌子、刷墙，没有叫校工过来搭手。 We painted the whole classroom ourselves, without asking the caretaker for help.
sceneCN: 这里 ourselves 是「靠我们自己」（第 3 个义项：by ourselves，表示不借助外人）；句意为一整间教室由我们自刷完，画面是空教室里围着一张旧桌子的几个人。

pos.zh: 我们自己；我们亲自；独自；私下地

derivatives.zh: 由 our 与 self 合写而成，是 ourselves 的单数形式，现仅见于王室或极正式的文字
古英语 self，义为「自身、本人」，是这一族反身形式的共同词干
由 self 与 same 复合而成，义为「完全相同的」

senses.title: The reflexive form of we
senses.definition: used as the object of a verb or preposition when the subject is we and the object is the same group of people
senses.definitionCN: 当主语是 we、而宾语恰恰是同一群人时，用作动词或介词的宾语
senses.example: We taught ourselves to play the guitar.
senses.exampleCN: 我们自学弹吉他。
senses.why: English sends an action back to its source with the self-words, so ourselves keeps the doing inside the very group that started it.
senses.whyCN: 英语用 self 这一族形式把动作送回它的来源，所以 ourselves 让「做」留在这群发起者内部；反身义就是「宾语与主语同指一批人」的直接结果。

senses.title: Used to stress that we personally did something
senses.definition: placed after we or at the end of a clause to insist that the people named did it in person
senses.definitionCN: 放在 we 之后或句末，强调所说的正是我们这批人亲自做的
senses.example: We built the whole shed ourselves.
senses.exampleCN: 整个棚子都是我们亲手搭的。
senses.why: The same form that bends the action back can also stand beside the subject as a pointer, so it adds weight instead of a new object.
senses.whyCN: 同一个能把动作折回自身的形式，也能站到主语旁边充当指示，于是它增加的是分量而不是新的宾语；强调义来自反身形式离开宾语位置之后的用法。

senses.title: Without help from anyone else
senses.definition: used in the phrase by ourselves to mean alone, or with no outside person assisting
senses.definitionCN: 用在 by ourselves 这一短语中，表示独自，或没有外人在旁帮忙
senses.example: We finished the repair by ourselves.
senses.exampleCN: 那次修理是我们自己完成的。
senses.why: If a group acts only within itself, no outside hand is involved, so the reflexive phrase settles into the meaning of unaided.
senses.whyCN: 如果一群人只在自己人内部使力，就没有外人的手参与，于是这个反身短语安定成「无人相助」的意思；独立义是从「不让别人插手」推出来的。

senses.title: Kept private among the speakers
senses.definition: used in between ourselves to mark that something is said in confidence and should not go further
senses.definitionCN: 用在 between ourselves 中，标记话语是私下讲的，不该再往外传
senses.example: Between ourselves, the plan has already been dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 私下说，这个计划其实已经取消了。
senses.why: A group closed upon itself is also a circle of trust, so the reflexive form can mark words meant to stay inside that circle.
senses.whyCN: 一个只向自己人闭合的群体，同时也是一个信任的圈子，所以这个反身形式能标记只该留在圈内的话；私密义由「闭合的小圈子」这一画面长出。

intro.en: Ourselves is our plus selves, a pronoun welded to the plural of self; the deeper origin of self is reconstructed rather than recorded.
intro.cn: ourselves 是 our 加 selves，也就是一个代词与 self 的复数焊在一起；self 更早的来源是重构出来的，而非有文字记录。

items.en: A reflexive stem usually reconstructed as sel-bho- is thought to lie behind the self-words, though the exact form remains uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，self 一族背后有一个重构为 sel-bho- 的反身词干，但确切形式仍不确定。

items.en: The reconstructed selbaz gave the Germanic languages their word for self, used both alone and beside pronouns.
items.cn: 重构形式 selbaz 为日耳曼诸语提供了表示「自身」的词，既可单用，也可放在代词旁边。

items.en: Old English set the pronoun and self side by side as separate words to say that the group acted on itself.
items.cn: 古英语把代词与 self 作为两个词并排使用，表示这群人把动作施于自身。

items.en: Middle English drew the parts together with the possessive our, and the plural selves won out so the form matched the plural subject.
items.cn: 中古英语用所有格 our 把两部分连写，复数形式 selves 占了上风，以便与复数主语相配。

items.en: Modern English fixed ourselves as the reflexive and emphatic form of we, leaving ourself to royal and very formal use.
items.cn: 现代英语把 ourselves 固定为 we 的反身与强调形式，只把 ourself 留给王室与极正式的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the other members of the same self-paradigm; the near-meaning group gathers plain pronouns and a phrase that carries the idea of acting alone.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个 self 系列里的其他成员；近义组收普通代词与一个表示「独自行动」的短语。

entries.definition: The reflexive form used when the subject is you.
entries.definitionCN: 主语是 you 时所用的反身形式。

entries.definition: The reflexive form used when the subject is they.
entries.definitionCN: 主语是 they 时所用的反身形式。

entries.definition: The reflexive form used when the subject is I.
entries.definitionCN: 主语是 I 时所用的反身形式。

entries.definition: A singular form once used with we in royal or formal speech and now rarely seen.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时在王室或正式文书中与 we 连用的单数形式，现已罕见。

entries.definition: The object form of we, a plain pronoun with no self idea.
entries.definitionCN: we 的宾格形式，是普通代词，不含「自身」之意。

entries.definition: The subject pronoun for the speaker together with at least one other person.
entries.definitionCN: 说话者与至少另一位构成的主语代词。

entries.definition: The possessive pronoun meaning belonging to us.
entries.definitionCN: 表示属于我们的物主代词。

entries.definition: Without help or support from anyone else.
entries.definitionCN: 没有别人帮助或支持；靠自己。

normalIntro.en: The word is our glued to the plural of self, so its hooks return to the group, to the self that turns back, and to the circle that keeps others out.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 our 与 self 的复数粘在一起，记忆钩子都回到这群人、折回自身的那个 self，以及把外人挡在外的圈子。

normal.en: Our means belonging to us, and selves is the plural of self, so the two halves say the same group twice.
normal.cn: our 意为属于我们，selves 是 self 的复数，两个部分把同一群人说了两遍。

normal.en: The self-forms are what English uses when the object of a verb is the subject itself, and ourselves fills that slot for we.
normal.cn: 凡是动词的宾语就是主语本身时，英语就用 self 这一族形式，而 ourselves 为 we 补上这个位置。

normal.en: Move the same form next to the subject and it stops being an object, which is how the emphatic use is born.
normal.cn: 把同一形式挪到主语旁边，它就不再是宾语，强调用法就是这样产生的。

normal.en: By ourselves keeps the group closed, so the phrase means alone, while between ourselves keeps talk inside the same circle.
normal.cn: by ourselves 把人群关起来，所以短语意为独自；between ourselves 则把话留在同一个圈内。

normal.en: Our own is the possessive echo of the same idea, since what belongs to us and what acts on us are both ours.
normal.cn: our own 是同一想法的所有格回声，因为属于我们的东西与对我们动手的东西都归我们。

abstract.en: A closed circle of people with no door for outsiders is the shape of by ourselves and between ourselves at once.
abstract.cn: 一圈人闭合成环、不给外人留门，就是 by ourselves 与 between ourselves 共同的形状。

abstract.en: A hand pointing back at the chest of the speaker shows the reflexive turn that the whole self-family marks.
abstract.cn: 一只手反指说话者的胸口，显示整个 self 系列所标记的那次折回。

abstract.en: A group carrying a table up the stairs with no one else on the steps is the word turned into a shared effort.
abstract.cn: 一群人自己把桌子抬上楼、台阶上没有别人，就是这个词变成共同出力时的样子。

examples.en: We taught ourselves to play the guitar.
examples.cn: 我们自学弹吉他。

examples.en: We built the whole shed ourselves.
examples.cn: 整个棚子都是我们亲手搭的。

examples.en: Between ourselves, the plan has already been dropped.
examples.cn: 私下说，这个计划其实已经取消了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥，塞住自己」——把外人挡在圈子外面，只留下我们自己。

root: 古英语以代词与 self 并列表意，中古英语把 our 与 self 的复数 selves 合写成 ourselves；self 一般认为上溯到原始日耳曼语 selbaz，更早的印欧形式不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a group turning an action back on itself; that picture splits into the plain reflexive, the emphatic pointer, the unaided group, and the circle of confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一群人把动作折回自身；这幅画面分出普通反身、强调指示、无人相助的一群，以及只对内的信任圈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several people carrying a table into a classroom, looking round to check that nobody else is helping.
core.cn: 核心意象：几个人自己把桌子搬进教室，四下张望，确认没有别人在帮忙。

branches.cn: 没人搭手、自己抬上楼的桌子

branches.en: two people talking with the door shut
branches.cn: 关起门来说话的两个人

branches.en: effort with no outside hand, once stressed and once described
branches.cn: 没有外人之手的出力，一次用于强调，一次用于陈述

intro.cn: 这个词是一个代词加上 self 的复数，嵌在英语一整套 self 形式之中，用来标记动作回到施动者本身。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.

definition_zh: 谜；神秘事物；神秘气氛；悬疑作品
definition_en: something that cannot be explained or is kept secret; the quality of being secret; a story built around an unsolved puzzle
core_image: 一只上锁的抽屉，里面的东西不翼而飞，锁却完好无损
scene: 书房的抽屉少了一封信，锁面没有撬痕，窗子也从里面扣着。 The letter vanished from a locked drawer, and the mystery is still unsolved.
sceneCN: 这里是「谜、无法解释的事」（第 1 个义项：找不到答案的事件）；句意为信从上锁的抽屉里消失，这个谜至今未解。图中可辨识物件：抽屉、锁、信、窗扣。

pos.zh: 谜；神秘事物；神秘气氛；悬疑作品

senses.title: Something that cannot be explained
senses.definition: a fact or event that resists explanation and keeps people guessing
senses.definitionCN: 无法解释、让人不断猜测的事实或事件
senses.example: The letter vanished from a locked drawer, and the mystery is still unsolved.
senses.exampleCN: 信从上锁的抽屉里消失，这个谜至今未解。
senses.why: The Greek noun named rites closed to outsiders; once the ritual frame fell away, what remained was a fact shut off from explanation, which is the everyday sense today.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词本指不许外人参加的仪式；仪式的外壳脱落之后，剩下的就是一个被挡在解释之外的事实，也就是今天的日常义。

senses.title: The quality of being secret or strange
senses.definition: an atmosphere of secrecy that surrounds a person, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 笼罩在人、地点或事物周围的神秘气息
senses.example: An air of mystery hangs over the house at the end of the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 巷子尽头那座房子笼罩着一层神秘气息。
senses.why: Because the word names what is withheld, it can also name the withheld quality itself, so a place becomes mysterious by carrying a mystery rather than by containing one.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词指被扣住不说的东西，它也能指那种被扣住的性质本身，于是一个地方不必真的藏着什么谜，只要带着谜的气息就显得神秘。

senses.title: A story built around a puzzle
senses.definition: a book, film or play whose plot turns on an unexplained event and its solution
senses.definitionCN: 以未解事件及其解答为主线的小说、电影或戏剧
senses.example: She reads a murder mystery every week before bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周睡前读一本谋杀悬疑小说。
senses.why: Readers wanted the pleasure of a puzzle that gets solved, so the word moved from the puzzle itself to the kind of book that delivers one.
senses.whyCN: 读者想要的是「谜被解开」的快感，于是这个词从谜本身转到了提供这种谜的那类书。

intro.en: Mystery reached English through Old French from Latin, and the Latin noun had already borrowed a Greek word for rites open only to the initiated.
intro.cn: mystery 经古法语、拉丁语进入英语，而拉丁语名词此前已借入一个希腊词，指只许入会者参加的仪式。

items.en: The verb myein meant to close, especially the lips or the eyes, and the sense of shutting away runs through the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 myein 意为闭合，尤指闭嘴或闭眼，这一族词始终带着「关起来」的意思。

items.en: A mysterion was a secret rite or teaching that insiders guarded from outsiders.
items.cn: mysterion 指内部人对外人守口如瓶的秘密仪式或教义。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as mysterium, where the sense widened from a rite to any hidden matter.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 mysterium，词义从仪式扩大到任何隐秘之事。

items.en: Old French mistere carried both the religious sense and the sense of a hidden truth, and passed the word to English.
items.cn: 古法语 mistere 兼有宗教义与「隐秘真相」义，并把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the puzzle sense, adds the atmosphere sense and the name of a literary genre.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「谜」义，又添上「气氛」义，并把词用作一类文学体裁的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective, the verb and other relatives on the same stem; the near-meaning group holds words for puzzles and secrets.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形容词、动词及其他同族词；近义组收表示谜题与秘密的词。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a name for closed rites and now covers any unexplained fact, the feeling around it, and the books written about it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是闭门仪式的名称，如今覆盖任何无法解释的事实、围绕它的感觉，以及以此为题材的书。

normal.en: The word goes back to Greek myein, to close the lips; a mystery is something someone keeps their mouth shut about.
normal.cn: 这个词可追到希腊语 myein（闭嘴）；mystery 就是有人闭口不谈的事。

normal.en: The plural is mysteries, with y changing to ies, the same pattern as story and stories.
normal.cn: 复数是 mysteries，y 变 ies，与 story、stories 的变化方式相同。

normal.en: Mystery is the noun, mysterious the adjective, mystify the verb; the family keeps one stem and changes only the ending.
normal.cn: mystery 是名词，mysterious 是形容词，mystify 是动词；这一族共用同一词干，只换词尾。

normal.en: An air of mystery needs no hidden fact; it can be produced by a closed door and a dim lamp.
normal.cn: an air of mystery 并不需要真藏着什么；一扇关着的门和一盏昏暗的灯就能造出它。

normal.en: A murder mystery is a genre label, so the word can name a shelf in a bookshop as well as a puzzle in a locked room.
normal.cn: a murder mystery 是体裁标签，所以这个词既能指密室里的谜，也能指书店里的一个书架。

abstract.en: A locked drawer with nothing missing teaches that a question can outlast its answer.
abstract.cn: 一只什么都没丢的上锁抽屉，说明问题可以比答案活得更久。

abstract.en: Every secret is a room whose door is shut from the inside, and every mystery is the light under that door.
abstract.cn: 每个秘密都是从里面关上的房间，而每个谜都是门缝下透出的光。

abstract.en: A word that names a closed rite ends up naming the pleasure of watching a lock be picked.
abstract.cn: 一个命名闭门仪式的词，最后用来命名「看别人开锁」的乐趣。

examples.en: The cause of the fire remains a mystery.
examples.cn: 起火的原因仍然是个谜。

examples.en: He enjoys solving mysteries set in old hotels.
examples.cn: 他喜欢破解以老旅馆为背景的谜案。

examples.en: Her sudden departure is shrouded in mystery.
examples.cn: 她的突然离开笼罩在神秘之中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯特瑞」——秘密被锁在密室里，就成了谜；mystery 就是谜。

root: 希腊语 myein（闭口、闭眼）派生的 mysterion（秘仪）经拉丁语 mysterium、古法语 mistere 进入英语；一般认为核心是「对外人闭合」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fact kept behind a closed door; the senses extend to the atmosphere such a fact creates and to stories built on solving it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被关在门后的事实；义项扩展到这种事实造成的气氛，以及以解开它为骨架的故事。

core.cn: 核心意象：锁完好无损，抽屉却开着，里面的东西不见了。

latinIntro.en: Latin carried the Greek noun into mysterium and also used the plural mysteria for the rites themselves.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词带入 mysterium，也用复数 mysteria 指仪式本身。

senses.definition: material that is no longer wanted and is thrown away
senses.definitionCN: 不再需要、要被丢掉的东西
senses.example: Rotten vegetables went straight into the garbage.
senses.exampleCN: 烂掉的蔬菜被直接丢进了垃圾里。
senses.why: The word names the unwanted remainder of daily life, the base sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名日常生活中被淘汰的部分，是基础义项。

senses.title: Worthless speech or writing
senses.definition: talk or writing that is silly, wrong, or without value
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢、错误或毫无价值的言语或文字
senses.example: That report is pure garbage, full of copied lines.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告纯粹是垃圾，全是抄袭的句子。
senses.why: Waste is judged, then words judged worthless follow the same bin image.
senses.whyCN: 垃圾是被评判的废物，无价值的言语沿用同一只「桶」的画面。

senses.title: Useless data in computing
senses.definition: input or output that a program cannot use sensibly
senses.definitionCN: 程序无法有效处理的输入或输出
senses.example: The crash was caused by garbage in the file.
senses.exampleCN: 崩溃是由文件里的无效数据引起的。
senses.why: Machines mirror kitchens: what no one can use is garbage there too.
senses.whyCN: 机器映照厨房：没人能用得上的东西在那里同样是垃圾。

senses.title: Refuse as a category
senses.definition: refuse collected from homes, seen as one stream
senses.definitionCN: 从家庭收走、被视为一股流的弃置物
senses.example: City garbage rises after every holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢节后城市垃圾都会增多。
senses.why: Many small wastes become one civic problem, and the mass noun holds them together.
senses.whyCN: 无数小废弃物汇成一个市政问题，不可数名词把它们拢在一起。

senses.title: To discard or dismiss
senses.definition: to throw away or reject completely, informal
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指扔掉或彻底否定
senses.example: They garbaged the draft and started over.
senses.exampleCN: 他们废掉了草稿，从头再来。
senses.why: Judging words as waste leads to treating them as waste, so the verb was coined.
senses.whyCN: 把言语判为废物便将其当废物处理，动词由此造出。

intro.en: Garbage began as a word for the waste bits of a butchered animal, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: garbage 起初指宰杀后禽畜的废料，更深的来源不确定。

items.en: The first attested sense was giblets and offal of poultry, with the root unexplained.
items.cn: 最早记录的义项是禽类内脏与下脚料，词根无法确解。

items.en: Middle English garbage named kitchen waste long before street refuse.
items.cn: 中古英语 garbage 在指街道垃圾之前早已指厨余废料。

items.en: An Old French garnete or garbage, mean scraps, is often suggested but not proven.
items.cn: 常被引证的古法语 garnete 或 garbage（意为碎屑）并无确证。

items.en: The sense widened from meat waste to all household refuse.
items.cn: 词义从肉食废料扩展到一切家庭废弃物。

items.en: American English added the computing and verbal uses, garbage in, garbage out.
items.cn: 美式英语加入了计算与动词用法，即 garbage in, garbage out。

note.en: Garbage, rubbish, and trash split by region, and garbage hides next to garage in spelling.
note.cn: garbage、rubbish、trash 按地区分工，拼写上 garbage 又紧邻 garage。

senses.title: To give light
senses.definition: to produce bright light
senses.definitionCN: 发出明亮的光
senses.example: Stars shine at night.
senses.exampleCN: 星星在夜间发光。
senses.why: This is the basic light sense.

senses.title: To beam
senses.definition: to send light onto something
senses.definitionCN: 把光照到某物上
senses.example: The sun began to shine through the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳开始从云层中照出来。
senses.why: Light moves from source to surface.
senses.whyCN: 光从光源移到表面。

senses.title: To polish
senses.definition: to rub something until it is bright
senses.definitionCN: 擦某物直到发亮
senses.example: He shone his shoes before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前他擦亮了皮鞋。
senses.why: Polishing makes an object shine.
senses.whyCN: 擦拭使物体发亮。

senses.title: To excel
senses.definition: to be very good at something
senses.definitionCN: 在某方面非常出色
senses.example: She shines in mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 她在数学方面很出众。
senses.why: Brightness becomes social excellence.
senses.whyCN: 明亮引申为出众。

abstract.en: To shine is to be seen without speaking.

definition_zh: 空气；天空；神态；播出
definition_en: the gas we breathe, or the sky, or a manner, or to broadcast
core_image: 早晨窗口吹进来的清风
scene: 清晨，窗户打开，一阵清风进来。 The air was fresh.
sceneCN: 这里 air 是「空气」（第 1 个义项：我们呼吸的气体）；句意为空气很清新。

pos.zh: 名词：空气；天空；神态；曲调

senses.title: The gas we breathe
senses.definition: the gas around us that we breathe
senses.definitionCN: 我们周围供呼吸的气体
senses.example: Open the window and let in some air.
senses.exampleCN: 开窗让一些空气进来。
senses.why: Air comes from Latin aer, the gas of the atmosphere, so its first sense is what we breathe.
senses.whyCN: air 来自拉丁语 aer，直接指大气里的气体，所以第一义是我们呼吸的空气。

senses.title: The space above the ground
senses.definition: the open space above the earth
senses.definitionCN: 地面上方的开阔空间
senses.example: The plane rose into the air.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机升入空中。
senses.why: The same gas fills the space overhead, which gives the sense of the air above us.
senses.whyCN: 同样的气体充满头顶的空间，就有了「空中」义。

senses.title: A manner or look
senses.definition: the way a person looks or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的样子或举止给人的感觉
senses.example: She had a happy air.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一种快活的神态。
senses.why: A person's mood seems to spread out like air, so air came to mean a manner or look.
senses.whyCN: 人的情绪像空气一样散发出来，air 于是指神态。

senses.title: A simple tune
senses.definition: a simple melody
senses.definitionCN: 简单的旋律
senses.example: The band played a simple air.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队演奏了一支简单的曲调。
senses.why: Old music words used air for a flowing melody, as if it moved like air.
senses.whyCN: 古音乐用语把流动的旋律叫作 air，仿佛它像空气一样流动。

senses.title: To broadcast
senses.definition: to send a programme out for people to hear or watch
senses.definitionCN: 把节目放出去供人收听或观看
senses.example: The school will air the film tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 学校今晚会播出这部电影。
senses.why: A programme is sent out into the air, so the verb air means to broadcast.
senses.whyCN: 节目被送到空气里传播，动词 air 就成了播出。

senses.title: A thin layer
senses.definition: a thin layer that forms on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 在表面形成的一层薄膜
senses.example: A skin formed on the warm milk.
senses.exampleCN: 热牛奶表面结了一层薄膜。
senses.why: Any thin surface layer can be called a skin.
senses.whyCN: 任何薄的表层都可以称为 skin。

intro.en: Skin came from Old Norse into English.
intro.cn: skin 从古诺尔斯语传入英语。

items.en: Skinn meant animal hide.
items.cn: skinn 意为兽皮。

items.en: The word replaced older English terms.
items.cn: 这个词取代了更古老的英语说法。

items.en: It named human skin as well.
items.cn: 它也开始指人的皮肤。

items.en: It spread to fruit and surface layers.
items.cn: 词义扩展到果皮和表层。

items.en: It became a verb meaning to peel.
items.cn: 它成为表示剥皮的动词。

note.en: Skin is compared with look-alike words and words for coverings.
note.cn: 把 skin 与形近词以及表示覆盖物的词作比较。

normalIntro.cn: skin 是身体的外层，也是任何薄薄的覆盖物。

abstract.en: Beauty is more than skin deep.

abstract.en: A thin cover can still protect a whole body.
abstract.cn: 薄薄的一层也能保护整个身体。

branches.cn: 身体被一层活的覆盖物包裹。

branches.cn: 热牛奶结出一层柔软的膜。

definition_zh: 城镇；市镇；城里；商业中心区
definition_en: a place with many houses, shops, and streets, larger than a village but usually smaller than a city
core_image: 一条街连着一条街，中间有广场和集市的聚集地
scene: 周六早晨，广场上支起了一排卖菜的棚子，熟人和陌生人混在一起走。 The whole town turns out for the market on Saturday.
sceneCN: 这里 town 是「城镇」（第 1 个义项：比村庄大、比城市小的人类聚居地）；句意为周六整个镇子的人都出来赶集。

derivatives.zh: 由 town 加 people 构成，义为「镇上居民」
由 town 加 -ship 构成，义为「镇区；乡」
由 town 加 -ie 构成，口语指「镇上人」

senses.title: A settlement larger than a village
senses.definition: a place where many people live and work, with shops and streets, but not as big as a city
senses.definitionCN: 许多人居住和工作的地方，有商店和街道，但不如城市大
senses.example: The town grew slowly around the river crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇子沿着渡口慢慢长大。
senses.why: The oldest sense is an enclosed settlement, and the fence that once made it a unit still shapes the idea of it.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是有围护的聚居地，那道曾使它成为一体的围墙至今影响着这个概念。

senses.title: The built-up centre as opposed to the countryside
senses.definition: the shopping and business part of a district, seen from the countryside around it
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区的商业与办事区域，相对于周围的乡村而言
senses.example: We drove into town to buy paint and a new lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 我们进城去买油漆和一盏新灯。
senses.why: People living outside mark the centre as their centre, so town becomes a place one goes into rather than a whole place.
senses.whyCN: 住在外面的人把中心当作自己的中心，于是 town 成为「要去的地方」，而不是一整块地方。

senses.title: The people of a town taken together
senses.definition: the inhabitants of a place regarded as one group
senses.definitionCN: 把某地居民视为一个整体
senses.example: The whole town came to see the fire engine.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇的人都来看那辆消防车。
senses.why: A place name can stand for its people, so the word shifts from streets to the crowd on them.
senses.whyCN: 地名可以代表居民，于是这个词从「街道」转到街上的「人群」。

senses.title: The place one belongs to
senses.definition: in phrases like home town, the place where a person grew up
senses.definitionCN: 如 home town 一类说法中，指一个人长大的地方
senses.example: He returned to his home town after twenty years in the navy.
senses.exampleCN: 他在海军待了二十年后回到家乡。
senses.why: Because a town holds a person's early life, it becomes a marker of identity rather than a mere location.
senses.whyCN: 因为镇子承载了一个人的早年生活，它就成了身份的标志，而不只是地点。

senses.title: Urban life as a manner
senses.definition: used before other nouns to describe customs and habits of urban living
senses.definitionCN: 放在其他名词前，描述城市生活的习俗与习惯
senses.example: Town life suited her better than the quiet farms.
senses.exampleCN: 比起安静的农场，城市生活更适合她。
senses.why: The noun in front position turns into a style label, describing a way of living rather than a spot on the map.
senses.whyCN: 名词放在前位就变成风格标签，描述的是一种生活方式，而不是地图上的一点。

intro.en: Town is one of the oldest English words and is related to Dutch tuin, garden, and to German Zaun, fence; it first meant an enclosed place.
intro.cn: town 是英语最古老的词之一，与荷兰语 tuin（园子）、德语 Zaun（篱笆）同源，最初意为「被围起来的地方」。

items.en: Old English tun means an enclosed piece of ground, a farm, or an estate, with a fence around it.
items.cn: 古英语 tun 指一块被围起来的地、农场或庄园，四周围着篱笆。

items.en: The same root gives German Zaun, a fence, and Dutch tuin, a garden, showing that enclosure was the core idea.
items.cn: 同一词根给出德语 Zaun（篱笆）和荷兰语 tuin（园子），可见「围护」是核心概念。

items.en: As settlements grew, tun came to mean a group of houses rather than a single farm.
items.cn: 随着聚居地扩大，tun 从单座农庄转指一群房屋。

items.en: By the later Middle Ages town is the ordinary word for a market settlement with a charter.
items.cn: 到中古后期，town 已成为指有特许状的集市聚居地的常用词。

items.en: From the seventeenth century town is often opposed to country, giving the phrase to go into town.
items.cn: 十七世纪起 town 常与 country 相对，于是有了 to go into town 这样的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words confused with town in spelling or sound, and the near-meaning group gathers kinds of settlement.
note.cn: 形近组收集拼写或读音易与 town 混淆的词，近义组收集不同类型的聚居地。

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the old meaning of an enclosed farm, from the compounds, and from the phrase of going into town.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「围起来的农庄」这一古老含义、复合词以及「进城」的说法入手。

normal.en: Old English tun was a fenced farm, so a town is first of all a place marked off by a boundary.
normal.cn: 古英语 tun 是围起篱笆的农庄，所以镇首先是划出边界的地方。

normal.en: German Zaun and Dutch tuin are cousins, both about enclosure.
normal.cn: 德语 Zaun 与荷兰语 tuin 是近亲，都围绕「围」这个意思。

normal.en: Town hall, town centre, home town: the word likes to stand in front of another noun.
normal.cn: town hall、town centre、home town，这个词喜欢站在另一名词前。

normal.en: Go into town works because the countryside surrounds it, not because the town has an inside.
normal.cn: go into town 成立，是因为乡村包围着它，而不是镇真有内部。

normal.en: The word is short and closed, just like the fence that started it.
normal.cn: 这个词短而封闭，正像最初围着它的那道篱笆。

abstract.en: Picture a fence, then houses inside the fence, then the fence forgotten and the houses still there.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆，篱笆里的房屋，后来篱笆被忘了，房屋还在。

abstract.en: Think of a square where every person knows three others by name but not everyone.
abstract.cn: 想一个广场，每个人能叫出另外三个人的名字，却不是所有人都认识。

abstract.en: A town is a village that got busy, before it became a city that got anonymous.
abstract.cn: 镇是一个忙起来的村庄，还未变成匿名的城市。

examples.en: Our town has one cinema and two bakeries.
examples.cn: 我们镇上有一家电影院和两家面包房。

examples.en: She went into town to post the letters.
examples.cn: 她进城去寄信。

examples.en: The old town is famous for its stone bridge.
examples.cn: 这座老城以石桥闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「趟」——一趟出去逛，街上到处是人，就是镇。

root: 古英语 tun（有篱笆围起的土地、农庄）→ 中古英语 town（一群房屋的聚居地）→ 现代英语 town（城镇）。同源词有德语 Zaun（篱笆）、荷兰语 tuin（园子）。

sensesIntro.en: From an enclosed farm the word grows into a settlement, then into the centre that people go into, then into the people who live there, then into the place a person belongs to, and finally into a style of life.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词从围起的农庄长成聚居地，再成为人们「进去」的中心，再指其中的居民，进而指一个人归属的地方，最后成为一种生活方式。

definition_zh: 英镑；磅；猛击；砰砰地敲；（心）剧烈跳动；捣碎
definition_en: the British unit of money; a unit of weight; to strike something hard and repeatedly; to beat with a heavy rhythm; and to crush something into a soft mass
core_image: 旧木桌上摊着一把硬币和一杆老秤，秤盘被压得往下沉
scene: 旧货市场快收摊了，摊主把一摞硬币推过来，又用手指点了点秤盘。 She paid three pounds for the brass scales and carried them home in her bag.
sceneCN: 这里 pound 指「英镑」（第 1 个义项：英国的货币单位）；句意为她花三英镑买下那杆黄铜秤，装进袋子带回家。图中可辨识场景：摊开在木桌上的硬币、被压低的秤盘、收摊前零乱的摊位。

collocations.zh: 按同等重量相比；同等水平下

derivatives.zh: 由 pound 加 -ing 构成，义为「重击；砰砰的响声」
由 pound 加表示人或物的 -er 构成，义为「捣击者；重达若干磅之物」
由 pound 加表示费用与计量的 -age 构成，义为「按磅计的重量或收费」

senses.title: The British unit of money
senses.definition: the standard unit of money in Britain, divided into one hundred pence
senses.definitionCN: 英国的标准货币单位，一英镑分为一百便士
senses.example: The ticket cost twenty pounds, which was more than he expected.
senses.exampleCN: 这张票要二十英镑，比他预想的多。
senses.why: English took the name of a weight for silver and used it for the money made of that weight, so the currency still carries a scale inside its name.
senses.whyCN: 英语把称银子用的重量名直接拿来指那个重量的银子所铸的钱，所以这种货币的名字里至今藏着一杆秤。

senses.title: A unit of weight
senses.definition: a unit of weight equal to about 454 grams, used in Britain and the United States
senses.definitionCN: 约合四百五十四克的重量单位，通行于英国与美国
senses.example: The recipe asks for two pounds of potatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份食谱要两磅土豆。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense in English: Old English pund weighed goods at the market long before it counted coins at the bank.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最老的义项：古英语 pund 早在银行数钱之前，就已经在市场上称货物了。

senses.title: To strike something hard and repeatedly
senses.definition: to hit something again and again with great force, usually with the fists or a heavy tool
senses.definitionCN: 用拳头或沉重工具反复用力击打某物
senses.example: He pounded the door until someone opened it.
senses.exampleCN: 他不停地擂门，直到有人来开。
senses.why: The beating verb is a separate Old English word, punian, probably imitative of blows; its spelling later merged with the weight word, but the force is its own.
senses.whyCN: 表示击打的动词另有来历，是古英语 punian，一般认为模仿打人的声响；后来拼写与重量词合流，但那股力道是它自带的。

senses.title: To beat with a heavy rhythm
senses.definition: to move or beat with a strong regular force, as a heart or a pair of running feet does
senses.definitionCN: 心脏或奔跑的脚步以强烈而规律的力道跳动、起落
senses.example: Her heart was pounding as she waited for the result.
senses.exampleCN: 等结果的时候，她的心怦怦直跳。
senses.why: Once the verb names repeated heavy blows, the body's own drum can borrow it, because a racing heart is felt as something striking from inside.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦指反复的重击，身体自己的鼓点就能借用它，因为心跳加速时，人感到的正是有什么在体内一下下撞。

senses.title: To crush something into a paste
senses.definition: to break something into small pieces or a soft mass by hitting it again and again in a mortar
senses.definitionCN: 用杵在臼里反复捶打，把东西碎成小块或软糊
senses.example: Pound the garlic with a little salt before adding the oil.
senses.exampleCN: 加橄榄油之前，先把蒜加一点盐捣碎。
senses.why: Crushing with a pestle is the same downward blow repeated in one small bowl, so the cooking sense keeps the action and changes only the result.
senses.whyCN: 用杵捣东西，就是在小臼里重复同一种向下砸的动作；烹饪义保留了动作，只换了结果。

intro.en: Pound carries two histories that ended up spelled alike: a Latin weight word that became money and mass, and an Old English verb of beating that probably copies the sound of blows.
intro.cn: pound 背着两段最后拼成同一个样子的历史：一个变成货币与重量的拉丁称重词，和一个很可能模仿打击声的古英语动词。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang and also to weigh, since goods were weighed on a hanging balance.
items.cn: pendere 既指悬挂，也指称重，因为货物是挂在秤上称的。

items.en: Pondo, short for libra pondo, meant a pound by weight, and this is the form that gave English the name of the unit.
items.cn: pondo 是 libra pondo 的省略，意为「按重量计的一磅」，英语里这个单位的名字就来自它。

items.en: Libra named both the scales and the Roman pound; its abbreviation lb and the crossed L of the money sign still stand for weight and for sterling.
items.cn: libra 既指天平，也指罗马磅；它的缩写 lb 与货币符号里那个带横杠的 L，至今仍分别代表重量与英镑。

items.en: Old English pund took the Latin weight word and used it for goods on the market and for silver by weight.
items.cn: 古英语 pund 接过这个拉丁重量词，既用于市场上的货物，也用于按重量计的银子。

items.en: A separate verb punian meant to beat or crush, probably imitative; Middle English merged its spelling with pound.
items.cn: 另有一个动词 punian，意为捶打、捣碎，一般认为带拟声性质；中古英语把它的拼写并入了 pound。

items.en: Modern English keeps the amount, the coin, the blows, the heartbeat and the mortar, all under five letters.
items.cn: 现代英语把这几种意思都留在五个字母里：分量、钱币、捶打、心跳与捣臼。

note.en: The look-alike group puts the word's own derivatives beside two spellings that only resemble it; the near-meaning group gathers money words and verbs of beating.
note.cn: 形近组把本词自己的派生词与两个只是拼写相像的词放在一起；近义组收货币词与表示捶打的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 重达若干磅的东西；捣击者。

entries.definition: Weight measured in pounds, or a charge made by weight.

entries.definition: To jump on something suddenly and seize it, as a cat does.

entries.definition: To push the lips forward in displeasure.

entries.definitionCN: 标准纯度的英国货币，尤指英镑。

normalIntro.en: Two strands meet in one spelling: a weighed amount that became money, and a repeated blow that became a heartbeat and a mortar.
normalIntro.cn: 两条线在一个拼写里相遇：一个被称出来的分量变成了钱，一种反复的击打变成了心跳与捣臼。

normal.en: Libra is why the abbreviation lb stands for a pound of weight and why the money sign carries a crossed L.
normal.cn: 正因为 libra，重量单位缩写写作 lb，货币符号里也带着一个带横杠的 L。

normal.en: Pondo meant by weight, so a pound was first a quantity of silver, and only later the coin made from it.
normal.cn: pondo 意为「按重量计」，所以一磅最早是一份银子，后来才指用这份银子铸的钱。

normal.en: The beating pound is a different word, from Old English punian, so no weight is hidden inside pound the door.
normal.cn: 表示捶打的 pound 是另一个词，出自古英语 punian，所以「擂门」那个 pound 里并没有藏着重量的意思。

normal.en: Compare heart pounding and rain pounding on the roof: both describe a heavy rhythm rather than a single blow.
normal.cn: 比较 heart pounding 与雨打屋顶：两者说的都是有节奏的重击，而不是单独一下。

normal.en: Pound the garlic names the same downward stroke a pestle makes in a mortar.
normal.cn: pound the garlic 说的正是杵在臼里那一下下的下砸动作。

abstract.en: A currency named after a weight reminds you that money once had to be put on a scale.
abstract.cn: 一种以重量命名的货币提醒人：钱曾经必须放上秤。

abstract.en: The word holds a scale and a hammer at once, and context decides which one you are holding.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时握着一杆秤和一把锤子，语境决定你手里拿的是哪一样。

abstract.en: A heart pounds in the same rhythm as a fist on a door, which is why one verb serves both.
abstract.cn: 心跳与拳头擂门是同一种节奏，所以一个动词能同时管这两件事。

examples.en: She paid three pounds for the brass scales.
examples.cn: 她花三英镑买下了那杆黄铜秤。

examples.en: He pounded the garlic with a little salt.
examples.cn: 他把蒜加一点盐捣碎。

examples.en: Her heart pounded as the plane touched down.
examples.cn: 飞机落地时，她的心怦怦直跳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「磅」的读音正好对得上；一磅重的东西砸下来砰的一声，pound 既是磅与英镑，也是猛砸。

root: 重量与货币义来自拉丁语 libra pondo（按重量计的一磅），经古英语 pund 进入英语；猛击义另有来源，一般认为出自古英语 punian（捶打、捣碎），可能为拟声。

sensesIntro.en: The senses split into two groups: a measured amount that turned into money, and a repeated heavy blow that turned into a heartbeat and a pestle.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项分成两群：一个被称出来的分量变成了钱，一种反复的重击变成了心跳与杵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brass balance on an old table, its pan pressed low by a heap of coins.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧木桌上一杆黄铜秤，秤盘被一堆硬币压得很低。

branches.en: coins counted twice on a market stall
branches.cn: 摊位上被数了两遍的硬币

branches.en: potatoes dropping one by one onto a scale
branches.cn: 土豆一个个落到秤盘上

branches.en: a fist landing on a locked door
branches.cn: 拳头一下下砸在锁着的门上

branches.en: a pulse felt in the throat while waiting
branches.cn: 等候时喉咙里感到的脉搏

branches.en: a pestle turning garlic into paste
branches.cn: 杵把蒜捣成糊

intro.en: A Latin family of weighing supplies the money and the mass, while the beating verb comes from Old English; English suffixes then build the noise, the tool and the charge.
intro.cn: 一个表示称重的拉丁词族提供了货币与质量义，表示击打的动词则来自古英语；英语后缀再分别造出响声、器具与按磅计的收费。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a unit of weight or money
weight or charge measured in pounds

definition_zh: 麻烦；困难；烦扰；使烦恼；疾病
definition_en: a problem or difficulty, or the act of making someone worried or upset
core_image: 水面被搅得浑起来，鱼看不见，连倒影都碎了
scene: 深夜，修车师傅蹲在路边，车前盖敞开着，车主来回踱步打电话。 The old car has given us a lot of trouble this year.
sceneCN: 这里 trouble 是「麻烦」（第 1 个义项：让人头疼的问题）；句意为这辆旧车今年给我们添了不少麻烦。搅浑的水面与来回踱步的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -some 构成形容词，义为「麻烦的；讨厌的」
过去分词形容词化，义为「困扰的；动荡的」
合成词，义为「惹麻烦的人」

senses.title: A problem or difficulty
senses.definition: a problem, difficulty, or unpleasant situation that must be dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 需要处理的难题、困难或令人不快的处境
senses.example: We had trouble finding the address.
senses.exampleCN: 我们找这个地址费了点劲。
senses.why: The verb behind the word means to stir up or disturb, and a stirred situation becomes a problem.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的动词意为搅动、扰乱，被搅乱的情形就成了麻烦。

senses.title: Worry or distress
senses.definition: a feeling of worry, anxiety, or unhappiness
senses.definitionCN: 担忧、焦虑或不快的情绪
senses.example: Her troubles seemed to lift after the call.
senses.exampleCN: 那通电话之后她的烦恼似乎散了。
senses.why: The stir that clouds the water also clouds the mind, so the word names inner unrest.
senses.whyCN: 搅浑水面的动荡同样会搅浑心里，所以这个词也指内心的不安。

senses.title: To cause someone worry
senses.definition: to make someone worried, annoyed, or uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 使某人担忧、不快或不安
senses.example: The noise troubled her all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那噪声扰了她一整夜。
senses.why: To trouble is to stir someone up, exactly as a stick stirs a pond.
senses.whyCN: trouble 就是把人搅动起来，正如一根棍子搅动池塘。

senses.title: Illness or a fault in a machine
senses.definition: an illness, or a fault in a machine or a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 疾病，或机器、身体某部位出的毛病
senses.example: He has heart trouble and walks slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 他有心脏病，走路很慢。
senses.why: A body or an engine that is not running smoothly is in a disturbed state, so it has a trouble.
senses.whyCN: 身体或发动机运转不顺就是处于被扰动的状态，于是有了毛病。

senses.title: Extra effort taken to help
senses.definition: extra effort that one takes in order to do something for others
senses.definitionCN: 为他人做事而额外花的力气
senses.example: She took the trouble to write by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她不嫌麻烦地手写了信。
senses.why: Stirring up effort on someone’s behalf is also a trouble, and the phrase keeps that effort visible.
senses.whyCN: 为别人搅起一番力气也是一种 trouble，这个短语把那份力气显出来。

intro.en: The word goes back through Old French to late Latin turbulare, to stir up, from turbare, to disturb.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语回溯到晚期拉丁语 turbulare（搅动），源于 turbare（扰乱）。

items.en: Turba means a crowd, a tumult, or a disturbance, and turbare means to throw into confusion.
items.cn: 拉丁语 turba 意为人群、骚动、扰乱，动词 turbare 意为使混乱。

items.en: Turbulare, to stir up, is formed on turba and gives the later Romance words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 turbulare（搅动）由 turba 构成，生出后来的罗曼语词。

items.en: Old French troubler means to disturb and also to make a liquid cloudy.
items.cn: 古法语 troubler 意为扰乱，也指把液体搅浑。

items.en: English borrows the noun and verb in the thirteenth century with both the literal and the mental sense.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入名词与动词，字面义与心理义一并带入。

items.en: Engineering and medicine give it the concrete senses of a fault and an illness.
items.cn: 工程与医学给了它「故障」与「疾病」两个具体义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin turb- family, while the near-meaning group names other problems and worries.
note.cn: 形近组汇集同出拉丁语 turb- 词族的词，近义组列出其他问题与烦恼的说法。

entries.definition: causing difficulty or annoyance
worried or full of conflict
full of sudden violent movement
to interrupt or upset someone
a matter that is hard to solve
the state of being hard to do
a state of anxious thought
a person or thing that annoys

normalIntro.en: The b turns to bl before the ending, and the word keeps the picture of stirred water.
normalIntro.cn: 词尾前 b 变成 bl，这个词始终带着搅水的画面。

normal.en: Troublesome adds -some and means full of trouble.
normal.cn: troublesome 加 -some，意为满是麻烦。

normal.en: Have trouble doing takes the -ing form after it.
normal.cn: have trouble doing 后面接动名词。

normal.en: Troubled is the adjective for a worried face or a troubled time.
normal.cn: troubled 形容人的忧色或动荡的时期。

normal.en: Turbulent and disturb share the same Latin root.
normal.cn: turbulent 与 disturb 共用同一个拉丁词根。

normal.en: The verb takes a direct object: the news troubled him.
normal.cn: 这个动词带宾语：那消息让他不安。

abstract.en: Picture a stick stirring a clear pond into brown.
abstract.cn: 想象一根棍子把清澈的池塘搅成褐色。

abstract.en: Watch the reflection break into pieces.
abstract.cn: 看倒影碎成一片片。

abstract.en: Wait until it settles, and the water is clear again.
abstract.cn: 等它静下来，水又清了。

examples.en: She had great trouble getting the machine to start.
examples.cn: 她费了好大劲才把机器发动起来。

examples.en: His back trouble keeps him from lifting boxes.
examples.cn: 他的背疾让他不能搬箱子。

examples.en: The question troubled her for days.
examples.cn: 那个问题困扰了她好几天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿不了」——鞋挤得穿不了，真是麻烦。

root: 拉丁语 turba（骚动）+ turbare（扰乱）→ 晚期拉丁语 turbulare → 古法语 troubler；同族有 turbulent、disturb

sensesIntro.en: The senses all come from a stirred thing: water, a mind, a body, or a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都来自被搅动的东西：水、心、身体，或机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stick stirring a clear pond until it is brown.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根棍子把清水搅成褐色。

branches.en: The plain problem sense, where affairs are stirred.
branches.cn: 麻烦义：被搅的是事情。

branches.en: The mind pair: worry felt and worry caused.
branches.cn: 心理一对：心里的烦与被搅起的烦。

branches.en: The concrete sense, where a body or a machine is disturbed.
branches.cn: 具体义：被扰动的是身体或机器。

branches.en: The effort sense, where stirring up work is meant.
branches.cn: 用力义：搅起的是一番力气。

branches.en: The problem sense again, where the water will not settle.
branches.cn: 再回麻烦义：水一时沉不下去。

intro.en: The word is Latin in origin, and the family around it is short but active.
intro.cn: 这个词源出拉丁，周围的词族短小却活跃。

latinIntro.en: Turba and turbare lie behind trouble, turbulent, and disturb.
latinIntro.cn: turba 与 turbare 支撑着 trouble、turbulent 与 disturb。

items.exampleCN: 他们生活在动荡的年代。

items.example: The turbine spins in the stream.
He was known as a troublemaker.
items.exampleCN: 他是出了名的麻烦制造者。
没有麻烦的一周很少见。

definition_zh: 访问；参观；拜访；探望；造访
definition_en: to go to see a person or a place, usually for a limited time and then come back
core_image: 提着礼物敲门，进屋坐一会儿，喝完茶再起身告辞
scene: 出差顺路，他拎着一盒点心敲开老师家的门，坐下喝了两杯茶才起身。 On his way back from the meeting, he stopped to visit his old teacher.
sceneCN: 这里 visit 是「拜访」（第 1 个义项：到某人那里去看望）；句意为开完会往回走时，他顺道去看望了老老师。提着礼物敲门、坐下又告辞的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 来访者；参观者
探访；视察；天罚的旧说法
来访的；客座的
重访；重新考虑

senses.title: To go and see a person
senses.definition: to go to a person and spend time with them, then leave again
senses.definitionCN: 到某人那里去，与他待上一段时间再离开
senses.example: On his way back from the meeting, he stopped to visit his old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 开完会往回走时，他顺道去看望了自己的老老师。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is simply the act of going to see someone; the coming and going is part of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是「前去看人」这一动作，来与去都包含在内。

senses.title: To go and see a place
senses.definition: to go to a building or town in order to look at it rather than live there
senses.definitionCN: 到某座建筑或城镇去看，而不是住在那里
senses.example: The class will visit the science museum on Friday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班星期五上午将参观科学博物馆。
senses.why: A place is visited the same way a person is: one goes there, looks, and comes away.
senses.whyCN: 地方与人一样被「拜访」：去一趟、看一看，然后离开。

senses.title: To stay somewhere for a time
senses.definition: to spend a period of time at a place as a guest rather than as a resident
senses.definitionCN: 作为客人而不是住客在某地停留一段时间
senses.example: My cousin came to visit for the whole winter holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 我表弟整个寒假都来家里作客。
senses.why: The sense stretches from a short call to a whole season, because what matters is being a guest, not the length.
senses.whyCN: 这层意思从短暂的拜访延伸到整个季节，因为关键在于是客人，而不在时间长短。

senses.title: To go to a doctor or clinic
senses.definition: to go to a doctor, dentist or clinic for help rather than having them come to you
senses.definitionCN: 自己去医生、牙医或诊所那里求助，而不是让对方上门
senses.example: You should visit a dentist if the pain lasts more than three days.
senses.exampleCN: 如果疼痛超过三天，就应该去看牙医。
senses.why: Diagnosis happens by going to the office, so the same plain verb covers a medical appointment.
senses.whyCN: 诊断发生在去诊所的过程中，于是同一个朴素动词也承担了看病的说法。

senses.title: To check a place or a site
senses.definition: to go to a place in order to inspect or check it, in official or technical use
senses.definitionCN: 为检查而前往某处，用于公务或技术语境
senses.example: Inspectors will visit the factory twice next month.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员下个月将到工厂巡查两次。
senses.why: Official inspection is a visit with a purpose, so the verb took on a checking shade without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 公务检查是一次带有目的的造访，于是这个词在不改变形态的情况下带上了核查的意味。

senses.title: To come upon someone in trouble
senses.definition: in older use, of trouble or punishment, to come upon someone
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指灾祸或惩罚降临到某人身上
senses.example: A great famine visited the region that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年大饥荒降临到这一地区。
senses.why: In older writing an affliction is said to visit people, as if it were a grim guest paying a call.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的文本里，灾祸被说成「造访」人，仿佛它是一位阴沉的不速之客。

intro.en: Visit comes from Latin visitare, to go to see, which grew from videre, to see.
intro.cn: visit 来自拉丁语 visitare（前去看望），而后者又由 videre（看）生长而来。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its frequent form visitare meant to go and see often.
items.cn: videre 意为看，其反复体 visitare 意为常常前去看。

items.en: In Roman use visitare covered visiting the sick and inspecting a province as well as private calls.
items.cn: 在罗马用法里，visitare 既包括探望病人、巡视行省，也包括私人拜访。

items.en: Old French visiter carried the verb into English, with the sense of paying a call.
items.cn: 古法语 visiter 把这个动词带入英语，含义是登门探望。

items.en: English widened it to buildings, towns and museums, all of which can be gone to and looked at.
items.cn: 英语把它扩展到建筑、城镇与博物馆，这些都可以去到并观看。

items.en: The noun visit appeared beside the verb, so English now says either pay a visit or visit.
items.cn: 名词 visit 与动词并行出现，所以现代英语既说 pay a visit，也直接说 visit。

note.en: The first group gathers the see-family, the second the words that describe different kinds of call.
note.cn: 第一组收「看」词族，第二组收描述不同性质造访的词。

entries.definition: The person who makes a visit.
An official or solemn visit, sometimes a punishing one.
To visit again, or to study something again.
Sight itself, from the same Latin verb to see.
To pay a short visit to someone.
To travel through a place looking at its sights.
To be present at an event rather than to look at a place.
To visit briefly and without an appointment.

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb to see sits under visit, visitation and vision, so the image of looking is never far away.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「看」这个动词藏在 visit、visitation 与 vision 之下，所以「看」的画面一直不远。

normal.en: Vis- means to see; visit is going there so as to see.
normal.cn: vis- 是「看」，visit 就是到那里去看。

normal.en: The visitor is the person; the visit is the call itself.
normal.cn: visitor 是人，visit 是这次造访本身。

normal.en: Pay a visit is the noun phrase; visit a friend is the verb.
normal.cn: pay a visit 用名词，visit a friend 用动词。

normal.en: Visitation is the heavy official version of the same act.
normal.cn: visitation 是同一动作里带有官方重量的版本。

normal.en: Vision shares the root and means the seeing, not the going.
normal.cn: vision 与它同根，指看的能力，而不是去的过程。

abstract.en: See a doorbell pressed once and a cup of tea poured.
abstract.cn: 想门铃被按一下，随后一杯茶被斟满。

abstract.en: Feel the short pause between greeting and leaving.
abstract.cn: 感受打招呼与告辞之间那段短短的停留。

abstract.en: Picture a guest chair that is never moved into the room.
abstract.cn: 想一把始终没被搬进屋里的客座椅子。

examples.en: We visit my grandmother every Sunday afternoon.
examples.cn: 我们每个星期天下午都去看望奶奶。

examples.en: The visitors were asked to sign the book at the door.
examples.cn: 来访者被要求在门口的本子上签名。

examples.en: A doctor visited him twice during the night.
examples.cn: 夜里医生去看过他两次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威兹特」——威兹特先生每次上门都提着礼物，一坐就是一下午。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看）→ 反复体 visitare（常常去看）→ 古法语 visiter → 英语 visit；同源词有 vision、visible。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts at going to see a person, then spreads to places, to being a guest, to seeing a doctor, to inspecting, and to trouble that comes like a visitor.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从「去看一个人」出发，再延伸到看地方、作客、看医生、巡查，以及像来客一样降临的灾祸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for a doorbell.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手按门铃。

branches.en: The person branch: a stop at an old teacher’s door.
branches.cn: 人的分支：在老师门口停一停。

branches.en: The place branch: a museum tour and a winter stay.
branches.cn: 地方分支：参观博物馆与整个寒假的作客。

branches.en: The medical branch: visiting a dentist.
branches.cn: 医疗分支：去看牙医。

branches.en: The inspection branch: inspectors arriving to check.
branches.cn: 巡查分支：检查人员上门核查。

branches.en: The old trouble branch: a famine that visits.
branches.cn: 旧的灾祸分支：饥荒的降临。

intro.en: Vis- is the Latin look; -it is the ending of the past participle, and ordinary English endings build the family.
intro.cn: vis- 是拉丁语的「看」，-it 是过去分词词尾，普通英语后缀再扩展出整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and its frequent form visitare are both well recorded, and so is the noun visitatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 及其反复体 visitare 都有文献记录，名词 visitatio 亦然。

items.example: The root is the seed of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是词族的种子。

items.example: It also gives vision and visible.
items.exampleCN: 它也给出 vision 与 visible。

items.example: The longer verb is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个较长的动词是直接来源。

items.example: It forms visiting, as in a visiting team.

definition_zh: 早的；早期的；早；提早；在初期
definition_en: near the beginning of a day, period, or process, or before the usual time
core_image: 天刚亮，鸟儿比闹钟先醒
scene: 天边刚泛白，街角面包房的灯已经亮起。 The baker arrived early to knead the first dough.
sceneCN: 这里 early 是「早、提早」（第 2 个义项：比通常时间更早）；句意：面包师提早到店揉第一团面。

derivatives.zh: early 加 ness 构成，义为「早；提早的性质」
early 的比较级，义为「更早地」

senses.title: Near the beginning of a period
senses.definition: happening near the start of a day, season, life, or history
senses.definitionCN: 发生在一天、一季、一生或历史的开端附近

definition_zh: 媒介；手段；媒体；中等的；灵媒
definition_en: a channel or means that carries something between two sides; also the middle point of a scale, and a person who claims to speak with spirits
core_image: 一只手把碗端在身前正中，不高不低，左右都不偏
scene: 戏台上，老艺人把一只小碗端在胸前，碗里盛着半碗水，不多不少，正好让台下看清碗底的纹路。 The old performer held the bowl at a medium height so that everyone in the yard could see the pattern inside.
sceneCN: 这里 medium 是「中等的、适中的高度」（第 3 个义项：处在两个极端之间）；句意为老艺人把碗端到中等的高度，好让院子里的人都看清碗里的花纹。

derivatives.zh: medium 的复数形式，专指报纸、电视、网络等新闻传播机构

由 medium 加表示身份状态的后缀 -ship 构成，义为「通灵的本领」

senses.title: A channel that carries something between two sides
senses.definition: something used to carry information, ideas or influence from one person or place to another
senses.definitionCN: 用来把信息、思想或影响从一方传到另一方的东西
senses.example: Speech was the first medium for passing stories down the generations.
senses.exampleCN: 口头讲述是把故事传给后代的第一种媒介。
senses.why: Latin medius means middle, and a medium literally sits in the middle, so the word starts from the gap it bridges rather than from the message it carries.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 medius 意为「中间的」，媒介就字面地待在中间，所以这个词的起点是它所连接的那道缝隙，而不是它运送的内容。

senses.title: Newspapers and broadcasters taken as one body
senses.definition: the press, television, radio and online outlets considered together as the channel that reaches the public
senses.definitionCN: 把报纸、电视、广播和网络平台合起来看，作为面向公众发声的渠道
senses.example: The story stayed out of the media for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事在媒体上压了三个星期没有露面。
senses.why: Once the channel is owned by companies and staffed by editors, the plural media stops naming a means and starts naming an industry with its own habits and power.
senses.whyCN: 当渠道归公司所有、由编辑操持，复数 media 就不再指某种手段，而是指一个有自己的习惯与权力的行业。

senses.title: Halfway between two extremes
senses.definition: of a size, amount or degree that lies between the largest and the smallest
senses.definitionCN: 大小、数量或程度处在一个区间的中间，不在两端
senses.example: Ask for a medium cup if the strong one keeps you awake.
senses.exampleCN: 如果浓的那款让你睡不着，就要一杯中杯。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the plain picture of the Latin root: a mark in the middle of a scale, chosen because neither end suits the purpose.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义保留了拉丁词根最朴素的画面：刻度中间的那一格，因为两端都不合用才选它。

senses.title: A person who claims to hear the dead
senses.definition: someone who says that messages from the dead reach them and that they can pass replies back
senses.definitionCN: 自称能收到死者的讯息、并把回话带回去的人
senses.example: The medium said a visitor from the other side had sat in the empty chair.
senses.exampleCN: 那位灵媒说，有位来自另一边的访客曾坐在那把空椅子上。
senses.why: Here the person again occupies the middle, standing between the living and the dead as a go-between, which is why this sense keeps the plural mediums instead of media.
senses.whyCN: 这里的人又一次占据中间位置，夹在生者与死者之间充当传话者，所以这个义项复数用 mediums 而不是 media。

intro.en: Medium is Latin for middle. English first borrowed it as a noun for a carrier, then let the plural media grow into the press and kept mediums for spirit talkers and middle sizes.
intro.cn: medium 是拉丁语中表示「中间」的词。英语先把它借作名词指承载之物，之后复数 media 长成「媒体」，而 mediums 留给灵媒与中间尺码。

items.en: Medius was the everyday Latin adjective for middle, used of anything placed between two others.
items.cn: medius 是拉丁语里表示「中间的」常用形容词，凡夹在两者之间的事物都用它。

items.en: The neuter form medium named the middle point of a space and also an element that stood between two others.
items.cn: 中性形式 medium 指空间的中点，也指介于另外两者之间的要素。

items.en: The verb mediare meant to be in the middle or to split something in half, and it produced a family of words about standing between parties.
items.cn: 动词 mediare 意为居于中间或把东西分成两半，派生出一族表示「居间」的词。

items.en: English took medium for whatever carries something else, such as air carrying sound or a person carrying a message.
items.cn: 英语借 medium 指承载他物的东西，例如传声的空气，或替人带话的信使。

items.en: The plural media came to mean the news industry, while mediums stayed with people who contact spirits; both plurals also name sizes that fall between small and large.
items.cn: 复数 media 逐渐指新闻业，mediums 则留给与亡灵沟通的人；两种复数也都用来指介于大小之间的尺码。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root for middle through several English words; the near-meaning group gathers words for a means of passing something on.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「中间」的拉丁词根串起几个英语词；近义组收表示「传递某物的手段」的词。

entries.definition: To stand between two sides and help them settle a dispute.

entries.definition: The power or means by which something is done.

normalIntro.en: The whole family circles one Latin idea, the middle, and the word keeps that position in every sense it takes on.
normalIntro.cn: 整族词都绕着拉丁语的一个意思——「中间」——打转，这个词每多一个义项，也仍然站在那个位置上。

normal.en: Medius is Latin for middle, so a medium is literally what sits in the middle between two sides.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 medius 意为中间，所以 medium 字面上就是夹在两方中间的那个东西。

normal.en: Media is the plural used for news outlets, which is why the word often appears with a plural verb in that sense.
normal.cn: media 是用于新闻机构的复数形式，所以这个义项常与复数动词连用。

normal.en: A medium shirt sits on the middle hook, between the small and the large, and the adjective follows the same picture.
normal.cn: 中号衬衫挂在中间那只钩子上，夹在小号与大号之间，形容词义用的是同一幅画面。

normal.en: Mediums, not media, is the plural for spirit talkers, because those people stand between two worlds rather than between two sizes.
normal.cn: 灵媒的复数是 mediums 而不是 media，因为这些人站在两个世界之间，而不是两个尺码之间。

normal.en: Mediocre comes from the same middle root and means only middling, a useful reminder that middle can also mean unremarkable.
normal.cn: mediocre 出自同一表示「中间」的词根，意为平平无奇，正好提醒人：中间也可以指不出众。

abstract.en: Every medium is a bridge, and a bridge is only noticed when it fails to carry anything across.
abstract.cn: 每个媒介都是一座桥，而桥只有在运不过东西时才会被人注意到。

abstract.en: A word for the middle ends up naming the press, the spirits and the middle shelf, because all three are places where two sides meet.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「中间」的词最后指媒体、亡灵与中间货架，因为这三者都是两方相遇的地方。

abstract.en: To choose a medium is to accept that the shape of the channel quietly shapes what travels through it.
abstract.cn: 选择一种媒介，就等于承认渠道的形状会悄悄塑造从中经过的东西。

scene: 火车再过十分钟就要开了。 We had to hurry to catch the last train.
sceneCN: 这里 hurry 是「赶快、匆忙赶路」（第 1 个义项：加快行动）；句意：我们得赶紧去赶最后一班火车。

senses.title: To move faster
senses.definition: to move quickly because time is short
senses.definitionCN: 因时间紧而快速移动
senses.example: Hurry, or we will miss the ferry.
senses.exampleCN: 快点，否则我们赶不上渡轮。
senses.why: The clock chases the body, so the feet must speed up.
senses.whyCN: 时钟在追人，所以脚步必须加快。

senses.title: To make someone move faster
senses.definition: to push another person to act or move faster
senses.definitionCN: 促使他人加快行动
senses.example: Do not hurry the children; let them finish.
senses.exampleCN: 别催孩子，让他们做完。
senses.why: The action points outward: your own rush is imposed on another person.
senses.whyCN: 动作指向外：把自己的急迫强加给别人。

senses.title: To do something too fast
senses.definition: to do something quickly and carelessly
senses.definitionCN: 匆忙且草率地做某事
senses.example: They hurried the vote through parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 他们让表决在议会里草草通过。
senses.why: Speed borrowed from moving is lent to doing: haste damages quality.
senses.whyCN: 移动的速度转借给做事：匆忙损害质量。

senses.title: Urgent need for speed
senses.definition: a state of needing to move or act quickly

senses.exampleCN: 匆忙中她把钥匙掉在了地上。

senses.whyCN: 动词变名词：急迫本身，常被指为失误的原因。

intro.en: Hurry first appears in late sixteenth-century English with an unknown origin, probably imitative of quick movement. It quickly displaced older words like haste in everyday speech.
intro.cn: hurry 首见于十六世纪末英语，来源不明，可能是对急促动作的拟声。它在日常用语中很快取代了 haste 等旧词。

items.en: No secure root has been found; some suggest a rare or dialect word or an imitation of bustling sound.
items.cn: 没有可靠词根；或出自罕见方言词，或为模仿忙乱声响的造词。

items.en: Hurry is first recorded around fifteen eighty, meaning to tremble or to move noisily and fast.
items.cn: hurry 约在一五八〇年首次记录，意为颤抖或喧闹而快速地移动。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the sense settled on moving or acting fast, and hurry up became the standard command.
items.cn: 十七世纪词义固定为快速行动，hurry up 成为标准催促语。

items.en: The noun hurry grew from the verb in the same period, and in a hurry became a fixed everyday phrase.
items.cn: 名词 hurry 在同期从动词长出，in a hurry 成为固定的日常短语。

items.en: The participle hurried turned into an adjective describing careless haste, as in a hurried decision.
items.cn: 分词 hurried 转为形容词，形容草率的匆忙，如 a hurried decision。

note.en: The look-alike group lists the hurry family and one false cousin. The meaning group gathers words for speed and haste.
note.cn: 形近组列出 hurry 词族与一个假表亲；词义组收集表示速度与仓促的词。

senses.title: Opposed to something

senses.whyCN: against 来自表示「相对、面对面」的词，与计划面对面站着，就是反对。

senses.title: In a contest with

senses.why: The Latin and French word for a turn gives the idea of going round a set of places and returning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语与法语中表示「转」的词带来了绕行一圈再回来的概念。

senses.title: A short visit with a guide
senses.definition: a short organised visit to a place, often with a guide
senses.definitionCN: 由人带领下对某处的短程参观
senses.example: The guided tour lasts about an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这次有导游的参观大约一小时。
senses.why: A short circuit of a building or a town is a mini version of a long journey, so the same word serves.
senses.whyCN: 绕建筑或城镇走一圈是长途旅行的缩小版，于是同一个词也就够用了。

senses.title: A series of performances
senses.definition: a series of public performances or appearances in different places
senses.definitionCN: 在不同地点连续进行的演出或露面
senses.example: The play goes on tour in the autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这部戏秋天开始巡回上演。
senses.why: Performers who travel from town to town follow a circuit, which is exactly a tour.
senses.whyCN: 艺人逐城而行正是走一条环线，那恰好就是 tour。

senses.title: A period of duty abroad
senses.definition: a fixed period of service in one place, especially abroad or in the army
senses.definitionCN: 在某地（尤指海外或军中）的一段固定服役期
senses.example: He completed a two-year tour in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 他在北方完成了两年任期。
senses.why: A period assigned in one post resembles a round of duty that ends and returns, and soldiers borrowed the word for it.
senses.whyCN: 派在一处的一段时期像一趟有始有终的差事，军人便借用了这个词。

senses.title: To travel around
senses.definition: to travel through an area or a country, visiting several places
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区或国家往来游览多处
senses.example: They toured the coast by train last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 去年夏天他们坐火车游了沿海一带。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb of going round, with the same image of a circle of visits.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为表示绕行的动词，仍是同一圈造访的意象。

senses.title: To take a visitor round
senses.definition: to show a person or a group round a place
senses.definitionCN: 带某人或某团体参观某处
senses.example: An old student toured us round the laboratories.
senses.exampleCN: 一位老学生带我们参观了实验室。
senses.why: Showing someone round is performing a tour for them, so the verb takes a person or a place as its object.
senses.whyCN: 带人参观就是替人做一趟 tour，故动词可接人或地方作宾语。

senses.title: On the road with a show
senses.definition: to go from place to place giving performances or making appearances
senses.definitionCN: 四处奔走演出或露面
senses.example: The singer toured Europe with a small band.
senses.exampleCN: 那位歌手带着一支小乐队巡演欧洲。
senses.why: This use fixes the word in the entertainment world, where the circuit of cities is a regular route.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法把词固定在演艺界，那里城市之间连成固定线路。

senses.title: A turn in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, a turn or a circular movement
senses.definitionCN: 较早文本中表示一转或环形运动
senses.example: The old clock's tour of the dial took a full day.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧钟的指针绕表盘一周要一整天。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a turn, and every later sense is a journey that comes back to its start.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「一转」，后来所有义项都是回到起点的行程。

intro.en: Tour goes back to Latin tornare, to turn on a lathe, and through Old French tour, a turn, to the modern sense of a circular journey.
intro.cn: tour 可上溯到拉丁语 tornare（在车床上转），经古法语 tour（一转）而到现代表示环行旅程的意思。

items.en: Tornare means to turn or to make round, and tornus names a lathe.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tornare 意为转动、使成圆形，tornus 指车床。

items.en: Tornus itself comes from Greek tornos, a tool for drawing circles.
items.cn: tornus 本身来自希腊语 tornos，一种画圆的工具。

items.en: Old French tour means a turn, a circuit, or a round of duty.
items.cn: 古法语 tour 意为回转、一圈或一轮差事。

items.en: Middle English borrows tour for a journey that goes round and returns.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 tour，指绕行一圈再回来的行程。

items.en: The performing tour appears in the eighteenth century as companies travel between towns.
items.cn: 巡回演出之义于十八世纪出现，因为剧团在城镇间往来。

items.en: Tourism and tourist are coined in the early nineteenth century from the same stem.
items.cn: tourism 与 tourist 于十九世纪初由同一词干造出。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for journeys and visits.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干上的词，近义组则汇集表示旅行与参观的词。

entries.definition: a person travelling for pleasure
the business of holidays and travel
a longer way round
a tall narrow building
entries.definitionCN: 塔，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an act of travelling from one place to another
a short visit to a place and back
a short group journey for pleasure
a long journey by sea or in space

normalIntro.en: These memories use the fixed phrases on tour and a tour of, the compounds with guide and package, and the way the word marks a circle.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用 on tour 与 a tour of 的固定搭配、与 guide、package 构成的复合词，以及这个词的「一圈」意味。

normal.en: On tour describes a performer or a team, while on a tour describes a traveller.
normal.cn: on tour 指艺人或球队，on a tour 指旅行者。

normal.en: Tour guide and tour operator both put tour before the noun it describes.
normal.cn: tour guide 与 tour operator 都把 tour 放在所修饰名词之前。

normal.en: A package tour bundles travel, hotel, and food into one price.
normal.cn: a package tour 把交通、住宿与餐食打包成一个价钱。

normal.en: Tourist and tourism add -ist and -ism to the same stem.
normal.cn: tourist 与 tourism 是同一词干加 -ist 与 -ism。

normal.en: Detour takes the prefix de- and means a turn away from the direct road.
normal.cn: detour 加前缀 de-，意为偏离直路的绕行。

abstract.en: Picture a bus circling a square and coming back to the same corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆大巴绕广场一圈，又回到同一个街角。

abstract.en: Think of a clock hand sweeping the whole dial and ending where it began.
abstract.cn: 想钟表的指针扫过整个表盘，最后回到起点。

abstract.en: A tour is a turn made large: the same returning shape, drawn across places instead of minutes.
abstract.cn: 旅行是放大的「一转」：同样的回环之形，只是画在地点上而非时间上。

examples.en: The orchestra is on tour in Asia for six weeks.
examples.cn: 乐团正在亚洲巡演六周。

examples.en: She gave us a tour of the new library.
examples.cn: 她带我们参观了新图书馆。

examples.en: We toured the island by bicycle in four days.
examples.cn: 我们用四天骑自行车环游了这座岛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「图」——出门前先摊开一张地图，画个圈就是 tour。

root: 拉丁语 tornare（转）→ 拉丁语 tornus（车床）→ 古法语 tour（一转、一圈）→ 英语 tour。同族词有 tourist、tourism、detour；拉丁 tornare 亦生出 turn 与之同源。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the journey round several places, then reduces it to a short guided visit, widens it to a series of performances and to a term of duty, and closes with the verb and the old sense of a single turn.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从周游数地的旅程写起，再缩小为有导游的短程参观，扩大到巡回演出与海外任期，最后收在动词用法与「一转」这一古老义项上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of visits that returns to the start.
core.cn: 核心意象：绕行一圈又回到原处的造访。

branches.en: The long journey and the old sense of a turn.
branches.cn: 长途旅行与古老的「一转」义。

branches.en: A short guided visit and the act of showing round.
branches.cn: 短程参观与带人参观的动作。

branches.en: Concerts on the road and touring with a show.
branches.cn: 巡回演出与随团巡演。

branches.en: A fixed period of service abroad.
branches.cn: 海外的一段固定任期。

branches.en: Travelling around an area.
branches.cn: 在一地区内往来游览。

intro.en: The word is a short borrowed stem; its family comes from -ist, -ism, -ing, and the prefix de-.
intro.cn: 本词是简短的借入词干，其词族来自 -ist、-ism、-ing 与前缀 de-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the root of turning and the words built on it.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出「转」的词根及其构成的词。

items.example: The English form drops the final vowel sound.
items.exampleCN: 英语形式丢了末尾的元音。

items.example: Tornus gives the root image of turning.
items.exampleCN: tornus 给出「转」的核心意象。
tourist 是为游乐而旅行的人。

items.example: Tourism is the trade of travel.
Touring means travelling on a circuit.
A detour turns away from the road.
